Appellant :- Sahid Ali And Another

Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the appellants is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no.2 as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

The instant criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the S.C./S.T. Act has been filed by the appellants- Sahid Ali and Mohd. Jakir Ali for grant of bail and to set-aside/quash the impugned order dated 04.07.2024 passed by the Special Judge, S.C./S.T. (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
Pratapgarh, in Bail Application No. 1654 of 2024 (Shahid Ali and another vs. State of U.P.), arising out of Case Crime No. 134 of 2024, under Sections 323, 504, 506, 376-D I.P.C. and Sections 3(1)Da,
3(1)Dha, 3(1)B, 3(2)va, 3(2)v of the S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Kotwali Dehat, District Pratapgarh,
during trial.

1 4.

Learned counsel for the appellants while pressing the bail appeal, submits that the appellants have been falsely implicated in this case, which is evident from the fact that in the year 2023 an F.I.R. was lodged by a woman of the village (victim of sexual assault) on 13.07.2023 at Police Station Mandhata, District Pratapgarh, against the husband and son of the victim of the instant case,
alleging that husband of the victim, namely, Munna Rao had entered into the house of the victim of that case and started molesting her and, thereafter, physically assaulted her and his son, namely,
Harsh has also assaulted the victim and the wife of the appellant no.2- Mohd. Jakir Ali, namely,
Shahjahan Bano was a witness in that case and the sole purpose of lodging of this F.I.R. (F.I.R. of the instant case) is to pressurize the wife of the appellant- Jakir Ali not to appear as a witness in trial court against the husband of the victim in that case.
5.

It is vehemently submitted that though, in the medical report of the victim of the instant case,
some bruises are shown to have sustained on forearm as well as on the breast of the prosecutrix/victim but having regard to the fact that the story, as narrated by the victim, is so improbable, these simple injuries have lost its significance, as no prudent person would believe that the son of the victim would ask her mother to accompany a person on his motorcycle whose wife is a witness in the "earlier case" lodged by a woman of the same village alleging rape and molestation against the husband and son of the victim of instant case.

6. It is vehemently submitted that the whole criminal jurisprudence revolves around the degree of probability and in the instant case the probability to ask her mother to be sit on the motorcycle of a person who is highly inimical, is a circumstance which would not be believed by any prudent person.
Appellants are languishing in jail in this case since 28.04.2024.
Criminal history of one case of both the appellants have been explained in para no.13 & 14 of the affidavit enclosed with the appeal.
Charge sheet in this case has been submitted and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail they may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

7. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel appearing for the opposite party no.2, vehemently,
opposes the submissions made by learned counsel for the appellants by submitting that the injuries sustained by the victim of the crime may not be lightly brushed aside and the injuries would itself speaks volumes that the prosecutrix of this case has been subjected to sexual assault and, therefore,
the appellants are not entitled to be released on bail.
8.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is reflected that the F.I.R. of this case has been lodged by the son of the victim alleging therein that on 27.04.2024 at about 6:30-7:00 pm. when he was returning from Pratapgarh his motorcycle ran out of the order and he along with her mother was returning at foot and during the course of their journey they met with appellants Jakir Ali and Shahid Ali and they asked the informant to leave their mother to the destination and thereafter the mother of the informant had accompanied appellants.
However, after 30-35 minutes her mother informed telephonically that she has been subjected to rape by the appellants and one unknown person.
The prosecutrix has been medically examined on the next day.
No injury has been found on her private part.
However, some bruises on forearm and on her breast were noticed.
The age of the prosecutrix, as per her own statement has been told, as 50 years.
The victim has supported the allegations of rape in her statements recorded under Section 161 and 164 Sahid Ali And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

2 Cr.P.C.

The appellants through supplementary affidavit filed today, has brought on record a copy of an F.I.R. bearing Case Crime No. 140 of 2023, which has been lodged by a woman of the same village against the husband and other son of the victim of the instant case and the wife of appellant- Jakir Ali, namely, Shahjahan Bano has been shown to be a witness of that crime.

The F.I.R. of that case pertaining to Police Station Mandhata, District Pratapgarh, which has been placed at Page No.11 of this supplementary affidavit filed today, would reveal that the charge sheet has also been submitted therein.

By referring to these documents, it is vehemently submitted by learned counsel for the appellants that no prudent person would believe that the son of the victim will permit her to accompany one of the appellant Jakir Ali on his motorcycle, who is the husband of the witness Ms.
Shahjahan Bano in the case filed/lodged against the husband and son of the victim of the instant case.

It is further the defence of the appellants that the instant F.I.R. has been lodged, so that the wife of the appellant- Jakir Ali, may not appear as a witness against husband and son of the victim of the instant case, in the earlier case.
Admittedly the age of the prosecutrix is about 50 years.

9. Keeping in view all the facts and circumstances of the case and specifically the circumstance that the families of prosecutrix of the instant case as well as of appellant no.2- Mohd. Jakir Ali were having high pitched enmity and the submissions which have been raised by learned counsel for the appellants that in all probability it may not be believed that the mother of the informant might have accompanied appellant Jakir Ali and also the fact that the appellants are in jail in this case since 28.04.2024 and criminal history of one case each of the appellants has adequately been explained, a case of bail is emerging in favour of the appellants.
The presence of the appellants may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.
10. Thus, for the reasons mentioned above, the impugned order passed by the special court is set-aside/quashed and the appeal filed by the appellants is allowed.

11. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, let the appellants- Sahid Ali and Mohd. Jakir Ali involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The appellants shall not contact the prosecutrix or any of the prosecution witness,
which shall be a sufficient ground for the trial court to cancel the facility of bail granted by this Court.
(ii) The appellants shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(iii) The appellants shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iv) The appellants shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
